changes.before: Create prefixes(id,prefix,size) with the first three characters and length of each name. Keep NULL as NULL, and preserve names.
changes.after: Count simple letters and take a short piece of text.

before: length(text) returns the number of Unicode code points before any zero character in ordinary SQLite text, not its rendered width or number of user-perceived graphemes. An empty text has length zero; length(NULL) is NULL. These examples use simple letters without embedded zero characters.

substr(text,start,count) returns a section of text. For a positive start, position 1 is the first character; count says how many characters to take. Asking beyond the end returns an empty text. substr(NULL,...) returns NULL. Parentheses hold the arguments and commas separate them.

Run this complete example in a fresh database.
```sql
CREATE TEMP VIEW shown AS
SELECT length('Lantern') AS size,substr('Lantern',2,3) AS piece;
SELECT *
FROM shown;
```

Change the supplied values and trace the result. This is a separate complete example.
```sql
CREATE TEMP VIEW shown AS
SELECT length('') AS empty_size,substr('Map',5,2) AS beyond,substr(NULL,1,2) AS missing;
SELECT *
FROM shown;
```
Application: Create prefixes(id,prefix,size) with the first three characters and length of each name. Keep NULL as NULL, and preserve names.
after: `length` counts the parts of a text value. For simple letters, this is the letter count. Empty text has length `0`. A missing value gives `NULL`, not zero.
`substr(text, start, count)` takes a piece of text. A positive start begins counting at `1`. The count says how many characters to take. Commas separate these three inputs.

Run this query:
```sql
SELECT length('Lantern') AS size,
       substr('Lantern', 2, 3) AS piece;
```
It returns size `7` and piece `ant`. Start at the second letter, then take three letters.

SQLite counts Unicode code points: the numbered pieces used to store text. One visible symbol can use several of these pieces, so this is not a screen-width measurement. An embedded zero character stops the length count. Taking text past its end returns empty text; taking it from NULL returns NULL.
Create `prefixes(id, prefix, size)` from `names`. For each name, take the first three characters and count its length. Keep missing values as NULL and leave the names unchanged.
